name: Standing Cable Horizontal Woodchopper
description: The standing cable horizontal woodchopper trains transverse-plane rotation of the trunk by pulling a cable handle from one side of the body to the other at chest height, challenging the obliques, transverse abdominis, and hip rotators in a movement pattern directly applicable to throwing, striking, and swinging sports. The cable provides consistent tension throughout the rotation in both directions — unlike medicine ball throws — allowing controlled loading at all points in the arc.

execution.starting_position: Stand side-on to a cable machine set at chest height. Grasp the handle with both hands, arms extended, feet shoulder-width apart.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the cable pulley to chest height. Stand far enough from the machine that the cable is taut at the start.
steps: Step 1: Begin with the handle in front of the shoulder closest to the cable stack, arms extended.
Step 2: Rotate the trunk away from the cable stack, pulling the handle horizontally across the body.
Step 3: Rotate until the handle is in front of the far shoulder, keeping arms straight throughout.
Step 4: Resist the cable and return to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Step 5: Complete all reps on one side before switching.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as the handle crosses the body. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows and turning a rotation exercise into an arm pull
Rotating from the hips only without engaging the trunk rotators
safety_considerations: Keep the spine neutral — do not laterally flex toward the cable
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Shoulder-to-shoulder rotation arc. Keep the spine tall throughout.
coaching_cues: Keep the arms straight — this is a torso rotation
Drive with the far hip to initiate the rotation
